messages:
maria.cs: Heads up — ACME (via ticket #4528) says tenant-scoped latency p95/p99 lines disappeared from their console after the metrics-router rollout an hour ago. They can still see p50/p90 and org-level charts but the tenant view is empty. Screenshot attached in the ticket.

alex.support: Can you paste the exact steps they took and the org_id? I'll ack to the customer and ask for a short repro. :thumbsup:

maria.cs: Customer repro steps: 1) Console -> Observability -> Latency SLOs 2) Select tenant = ACME (org_id=org_87ab3c) 3) timeframe = 1h 4) p95/p99 series show as empty/flatline. They included this query they ran in the UI: `metric_latency_ms{org_id="org_87ab3c",quantile=~"p95|p99"}` and returned nothing. Screenshot link: https://acme.screenshots/xyz (in ticket).

sam.eng-sre: Thanks. Quick checks: are the percentile series still arriving to kafka? Can someone grep the metrics-router output for org_87ab3c and quantile labels?

taylor.eng-platform: Deploy bot shows metrics-router v2.14 rolled to canary pool at +00:20, rollout to 25% traffic. We did enable a new transform flag in the router: `strip_sensitive_labels=true` and a whitelist that should have kept `org_id` — but it's possible the whitelist logic regressed.

maria.cs: Adding traces from the customer: they paged at 11:22 and first noticed after 11:30.

sam.eng-sre: I pulled logs from the canary instance handling tenant traffic. Snippet: ```
2024-05-03T11:28:41Z INFO metrics-router: received batch size=1200
2024-05-03T11:28:42Z WARN transform: label_filter matched, dropping labels=[tenant_id] reason="whitelist-miss"
2024-05-03T11:28:42Z DEBUG serializer: output_series_count=1135
```

sam.eng-sre: That WARN is the smoking gun — it looks like our label whitelist didn't include `tenant_id` (we use org_id -> tenant mapping), so percentiles that are sharded by tenant lost their tenant label and aggregated to org-level which explains org-level charts still present.

taylor.eng-platform: Repro locally by toggling `strip_sensitive_labels` + bad whitelist. Confirmed we accidentally replaced the whitelist during the refactor and `tenant_id` was removed. :facepalm:

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: metrics-router-canary rollout completed on host metrics-router-canary-3 at 2024-05-03T11:25:00Z.

sam.eng-sre: Short-term: option A rollback canary to previous image; option B push hotfix to re-add tenant_id to whitelist and flip canary config. Rolling back gives fastest customer relief. Thoughts?

taylor.eng-platform: I can flip canary back to v2.13 now if eng-sre wants rollback. Hotfix build + canary takes ~20m to verify. Given customer impact, I vote rollback.

alex.support: I'll tell ACME we're escalating to SRE and we plan a rollback now. Will give ETA 15-30m.

maria.cs: Please include that we'll follow up when we confirm p95/p99 reappear.

sam.eng-sre: Rolling back metrics-router canary to v2.13 on canary hosts now. Commands: ```
# rollback
kubectl -n infra set image deployment/metrics-router metrics-router=registry/redwood/metrics-router:v2.13
kubectl rollout status deploy/metrics-router -n infra
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated by sam.eng-sre at 2024-05-03T11:35:12Z

sam.eng-sre: Rollback completed on canary hosts. Waiting 60s for pipelines to drain.

sam.eng-sre: Quick check: ran the same query against the time-series store for org_87ab3c: now returns p95/p99 series. Example: `metric_latency_ms{org_id="org_87ab3c",quantile="p99"}` -> 142ms.

maria.cs: I pinged ACME: they confirm lines reappeared and dashboards look normal. They said thanks. Closing loop in ticket.

alex.support: Great. Can we get a postmortem/CL with the root cause and remediation to prevent whitelist regressions? I'll attach to the support ticket.

taylor.eng-platform: I'll own the postmortem and a config safety test to run in CI that asserts tenant_id/ org_id survive transforms. Assigning to me + sam.

sam.eng-sre: Adding follow-ups: 1) revert the refactor branch that touched the whitelist logic 2) add unit test + e2e canary test 3) run a sweep for other labels accidentally removed.

maria.cs: Thanks team — customer happy for now. Please post the postmortem link in this thread when ready so I can mark ticket resolved. :pray:
